surface_claims.note: The Transmittals response alone does not provide a stable source-document lineage identity. No lineage was inferred from the issued version identifier by URN splitting, suffix removal, reconstruction, canonicalisation or pattern inference.
The issued document version identity was returned as a field by the Transmittals documents read.
ITEM_1 is the Data Management item resource, returned directly as a field by a first-party Data Management read. It was not derived from any version identifier.
The lineage tip relation was returned directly by Data Management, not inferred from client-side ordering.

Established during the controlled live run while both surface operands were simultaneously available. This proves an exact version relationship only; it does not make the Transmittals surface a lineage source.

proofs.statement: The version issued by the completed transmittal is the same exact version identity as the corresponding version in the source Data Management lineage.
proofs.note: The freeze retains one canonical VERSION_1 identity rather than two independent surface operands, so this historically established equality is not recomputable from the frozen evidence alone.

proofs.statement: The current tip version of the source Data Management lineage is the same exact version identity as the second returned version.
proofs.note: Recorded alongside the current_tip_relation surface claim. The freeze retains the canonical VERSION_2 identity rather than the independent tip operand, so this historically established equality is not recomputable from the frozen evidence alone.

proofs.statement: The version issued by the transmittal and the current tip version of the source lineage are different exact version identities.
proofs.note: Both canonical version identities survive independently in the frozen private evidence, so this inequality can be independently re-checked there.

evidence_integrity.note: Provenance classes describe how each retained alias is trusted. They describe evidence provenance only, never Autodesk resource semantics, and permit no reconstruction, inference or derivation of an identifier.

aliases.note: Provenance is EQUALITY_VERIFIED_LATER_RESULT because the original establishing response aged out. That concerns the surviving evidence source only; the item identity itself was returned first-party by Data Management.

governance_checks.statement: Transmittals-surface stable lineage is recorded only as not_proven.
No lineage was inferred from a Transmittals version identifier by any client-side transformation.
ITEM_1 is recorded as proven item/lineage identity only because it was returned directly by the first-party Data Management resource.
Cross-surface version equality is claimed only from byte-for-byte exact comparison, and no raw operand is published.
No raw Autodesk numeric version property is published; version structure uses aliases plus count and has_more.
Every retained alias carries an evidence-provenance class, and classes weaker than ORIGINATING_RESULT are disclosed rather than upgraded.
The verdict is scoped to the controlled fixture and makes no universal, tenant-wide, gate-wide or phase-completion claim.
Teaching-scenario placement is recorded separately from capture provenance; the scenario project is not asserted to contain the fixture.
This artifact was generated separately from the private capture; the private file was not sanitised in place.

warnings.message: The strict originating-result preflight did not pass: two establishing responses had aged out of the capture session. An explicit provenance policy accepted verified surviving values under named classes, and no recovery read was performed.

This alias-only artifact records historically established proof outcomes. Raw operands are deliberately excluded, so no proof is recomputable from the public artifact. That is intentional and is not an evidence defect.
